subject: Banking
title: Central Banks and Climate Change
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Central Banks and Climate Change.

hook.text: Should central banks fight climate change? The ECB and Bank of England say yes. The Fed says it's not their job.

buildup.text: The ECB now considers climate risk in its bond purchases. It buys fewer bonds from heavy carbon emitters.

discovery.text: Climate change creates financial risk: stranded assets, extreme weather losses.

twist.text: Critics argue central banks should stick to inflation and employment.

climax.text: As climate risk becomes financial risk, central banks are drawn in.

punchline.text: Climate risk is financial risk. Central banks are getting involved regardless.

quiz.question: How does the ECB address climate change?
options: It considers climate risk in bond purchases

details.summary: Central banks are increasingly treating climate change as a financial stability risk, incorporating environmental stress tests and pushing banks to disclose their exposure to fossil fuel assets and climate-related losses.
details.whyItMatters: Climate change threatens to strand trillions in fossil fuel assets and cause massive insurance losses. Central banks must decide whether their mandate extends to preventing a climate-driven financial crisis.
takeaways: The Network for Greening the Financial System has over 120 central bank members
Climate stress tests assess bank portfolios against warming scenarios
Critics argue central banks are exceeding their monetary policy mandates

faq.question: Why should central banks care about climate change?
faq.answer: Climate disasters can cause massive loan defaults, insurance failures, and asset price collapses. Central banks responsible for financial stability must assess whether climate risks could trigger a systemic financial crisis.

faq.question: Do climate stress tests actually change bank behavior?
faq.answer: Early evidence suggests banks are beginning to reduce fossil fuel exposure in response to stress test results and disclosure requirements. However, critics argue the tests use overly optimistic scenarios and lack enforcement.
